READING

**The fixed cost first**

Both courses carry the same GBP 27,072 in learning-curve remakes. That figure drops out of the comparison and I will set it aside.

---

**What KIRKBANE costs above baseline**

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Overtime | GBP 44,000 |
| Crossing remakes | GBP 0 |
| **Total incremental** | **GBP 44,000** |

No cases cross systems because everyone moves on the same day, so crossing remakes are structurally zero. That is KIRKBANE's one genuine financial advantage.

---

**What AVENSWOOD costs above baseline**

Overtime is zero. The question is the crossing-remake bill.

The pilot gives the only empirical anchor: 2 technicians on the new system alongside 10 on the old produced 40 crossing remakes in 4 months — 10 per month.

Crossing remakes require a case to touch technicians on both sides of the boundary. The most natural model is that the rate scales with the *product* of new-system and old-system headcount, because the chance of a case spanning the boundary rises with both populations. Using the pilot to calibrate:

- Pilot: 2 × 10 = 20 exposure-units → 10 remakes/month → **0.50 remakes/month per exposure-unit**

Under AVENSWOOD the composition changes each quarter:

| Period | New | Old | Product | Months | Remakes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jan–Apr 2027 | 3 | 7 | 21 | 3 | 31.5 |
| Apr–Jul 2027 | 6 | 4 | 24 | 3 | 36.0 |
| Jul–Oct 2027 | 9 | 1 | 9 | 3 | 13.5 |
| **Total** | | | | | **81** |

81 remakes × GBP 96 = **GBP 7,776**

This model could be wrong in either direction. If crossing remakes scale simply with the number of new-system technicians (a more generous assumption for KIRKBANE's case), the total reaches about 270 remakes × GBP 96 = **GBP 25,920** — the most pessimistic defensible estimate. I will use the range GBP 8,000–26,000.

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Overtime | GBP 0 |
| Crossing remakes | GBP 8,000–26,000 |
| **Total incremental** | **GBP 8,000–26,000** |

---

**The financial gap**

KIRKBANE costs GBP 44,000 in incremental spending above baseline.  
AVENSWOOD costs GBP 8,000–26,000 in incremental spending above baseline.

AVENSWOOD is cheaper by GBP 18,000–36,000. The crossing-remake estimate would have to be almost entirely driven by the most aggressive linear model *and* run well above even that ceiling before the crossing cost closed the gap with GBP 44,000. There is no plausible arithmetic that makes KIRKBANE cheaper.

---

**Completion dates**

KIRKBANE completes the crossing by 2027-12-04.  
AVENSWOOD's last technician crosses on 2027-10-04 — two months *earlier*.  
Both leave substantial margin before the 2028-06-30 support deadline. This edge belongs to AVENSWOOD.

---

**Quality and practice relationships**

Under KIRKBANE, all 40 practices see the 11.4% remake rate at the same moment in January 2027. That is the laboratory's entire output dropping from 3.1% to 11.4% simultaneously, for an extended period. Practices compare notes. Losing even one or two practices to a competitor during that window would cost more than GBP 44,000 in lifetime revenue.

Under AVENSWOOD, three-quarters of the bench stays at 3.1% throughout. The elevated remake rate is visible in roughly one-quarter of work at any given time, spread across 40 practices rather than concentrated in a single pulse. The signal is weaker and the lab's overall quality reputation remains largely intact.

---

**The dual-library risk**

AVENSWOOD runs two shade and material libraries for nine months, and practices work from those. The pilot showed 40 crossing remakes in four months attributable partly to this — that cost is already captured in the crossing-remake estimate above. The dual library is a genuine operational friction, but it is not an unmanaged surprise: the pilot demonstrated it is survivable and quantifiable.

---

**Summary comparison (incremental costs only)**

| | KIRKBANE | AVENSWOOD |
|---|---|---|
| Overtime | GBP 44,000 | GBP 0 |
| Crossing remakes | GBP 0 | GBP 8,000–26,000 |
| Dual-library risk | None | Manageable; captured above |
| Practice quality exposure | All 40 practices, simultaneous | ~25% of work at any time |
| Completes | Dec 2027 | Oct 2027 |
| **Net incremental** | **GBP 44,000** | **GBP 8,000–26,000** |

AVENSWOOD wins on cost in every scenario, finishes sooner, and limits the reputational exposure to practices. KIRKBANE's only genuine structural advantage — no crossing remakes — is worth at most GBP 26,000 under the most punishing model, which still leaves AVENSWOOD GBP 18,000 ahead.

---

CALL
AVENSWOOD

GROUNDS
The GBP 44,000 overtime cost of KIRKBANE exceeds the crossing-remake bill of AVENSWOOD under every plausible scaling model, and AVENSWOOD additionally protects three-quarters of output quality throughout the transition and finishes two months sooner.
